claims.text: The target system is a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy, exemplified by equiatomic Ta-Mo-Nb-W-V.
No machine-learning potential is currently available that is trained for the specific multicomponent liquid structure of the target alloy.
Full DFT thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive for this system.
Standard EAM potentials inadequately represent complex liquid structures in multicomponent refractory alloys.
Liquid short-range order and chemical clustering are important to accurate free-energy predictions in multicomponent refractory systems.
HEAs can exhibit high-temperature short-range order and substantial chemical clustering.
A GAP- or SNAP-type local-environment MLP can capture the liquid short-range order and chemical clustering missed by EAM.
An MLP trained on liquid configurations can learn the complex nonlinear interactions among Ta, Mo, Nb, W, and V.
Training on liquid configurations will allow the MLP to reproduce ab initio liquid structure factors and radial distribution functions accurately.
Approximately 1000 DFT liquid configurations from small-cell high-temperature ab initio MD are sufficient to train the proposed MLP.
A thermodynamic-perturbation calculation based on a small set of MLP-generated high-energy liquid configurations can replace integration over the full phase space.
The perturbation scheme estimates the liquid-solid free-energy difference using an MLP while avoiding full DFT phase-space sampling.
The efficiency gain arises because sampling is focused on the liquid-solid interface rather than the entire phase space.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10 to 100 relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method will predict the free-energy difference to within 5% of the DFT reference.
The method will resolve subtle free-energy differences between competing BCC and B2 solid phases.
The method is valid for Ta-based refractory BCC HEAs containing five to seven principal elements.
The trained potential may not transfer to alloys with significant covalent bonding, magnetic effects, or compositions outside its training set.
The accuracy of the perturbation calculation is limited by the quality, diversity, and phase-space coverage of the liquid training data.
Likely MLP failure modes include extrapolation errors, training-set bias, and slow sampling in systems with high energy barriers.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the perturbation samples a small set of high-energy liquid configurations, whereas the mechanism says the cost reduction comes from focusing on the liquid-solid interface. These are different sampling domains, and no connection between them is specified.

The MLP is described as being trained specifically on liquid configurations, but it is then used for liquid-solid free energies and BCC-versus-B2 solid free-energy differences without stating how solid configurations are represented or validated.
